# Background

A section of the South Fork Clearwater River near milepost (MP) 28 has been identified as a potential migration barrier for adult steelhead, particularly during periods of elevated discharge. High stream velocities within this reach are thought to impede, and some cases prevent, upstream migration, thereby limiting access to spawning habitat in the upper mainstem and its tributaries. Previous hydraulic modeling suggested that at least one feature within the reach produces velocities exceeding the burst swimming capacity of a 90-cm steelhead when discharge surpasses approximately 1,000 cfs [@Timm2017; @Timm2018]. Earlier observations by Nez Perce Tribe (NPT) staff further suggested that barrier conditions may begin to develop at flows exceeding roughly 600 cfs, based on measurements from the former Elk City gage. Supporting these concerns, radio telemetry data collected from 2013–2017 [@Cleary2019] indicated that relatively few steelhead spawned upstream of river kilometer (rkm) 71, which corresponds to the location of the suspected high-velocity reach (Figure \@ref(fig:loc-by-rkm)).

```{r loc-by-rkm, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Estimated spawning locations for adult steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River from a radio telemetry study conducted in 2013 - 2017."}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures/sthd_spawn_location_by_rkm.png"))

```

This report presents a preliminary assessment of adult steelhead passage at the suspected velocity barrier using detections of PIT-tagged fish. Key detection sites include SC3, located downstream of the suspected barrier, and SC4, located upstream. The analysis incorporates adults PIT-tagged at Bonneville and Lower Granite dams, as well as juveniles tagged at multiple locations, including within the South Fork Clearwater River watershed.

The primary objective was to evaluate whether adult steelhead detected at SC3 were subsequently detected at SC4, thereby indicating successful upstream passage through the high-velocity reach. We also examined how factors such as juvenile release location (relative to the reach) and river discharge influenced “conversion” rates between sites. In this context, conversion rate refers to the proportion of adults successfully transitioning between key upstream migration points and serves as a proxy for both survival and passage success. Although the primary focus was steelhead, PIT-tag detections of adult spring/summer Chinook salmon were also evaluated for comparison.

To support this evaluation, the number of PIT-tagged juvenile steelhead released into Newsome Creek was increased beginning in 2022 (Table \@ref(tab:juv-releases)). The first 1-ocean adults from these releases returned to spawn in spring 2024; with two-ocean adults first returning in 2025.

```{r juv-releases, tab.cap = "Number of PIT-tagged juveniles released within Newsome Creek releases by year, including years that each release group will return to spawn."}
juv_rel_df = read_csv(
  file = here("data/derived_data/tag_detail/Tagging Detail 20260526.csv"),
  show_col_types = F
) %>%
  clean_names()

juv_rel_df %>%
  transmute(
    rel_site = str_sub(release_site_name, 1, 6),
    release_year = release_year_yyyy,
    srr_code,
    mark_count
  ) %>%
  filter(
    srr_code == "32H",
    rel_site == "NEWSOC"
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mark_count = sum(mark_count),
    .by = c(rel_site, release_year)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sw_age_1_sy = release_year + 2,
    sw_age_2_sy = release_year + 3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    `Release Site` = rel_site,
    `Release Year` = release_year,
    `Tag Count`    = mark_count,
    `SW Age 1 SY`  = sw_age_1_sy,
    `SW Age 2 SY`  = sw_age_2_sy
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = T,
    align = "ccccc",
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = F,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

```{r prep-gage-data}
sf_gage_fit_df = sf_gage_df %>%
  select(site_no, date, daily_mean_cfs) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = site_no,
    values_from = daily_mean_cfs
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(`13337500`) & !is.na(`13338500`)
  )

sf_gage_lm = lm(`13337500` ~ `13338500`, data = sf_gage_fit_df)
#summary(sf_gage_lm)

# create new gage data with estimated cfs at Elk City gage when missing
sf_gage_pred_df = sf_gage_df %>%
  select(site_no, date, daily_mean_cfs) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = site_no,
    values_from = daily_mean_cfs
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pred_elk_city       = predict(sf_gage_lm, newdata = pick(`13338500`)),
    cfs_source_elk_city = if_else(is.na(`13337500`), "predicted", "observed"),
    `13337500` = coalesce(`13337500`, pred_elk_city)
  ) %>%
  select(-pred_elk_city) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(`13337500`, `13338500`),
    names_to  = "site_no",
    values_to = "daily_mean_cfs"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    source = case_when(
      site_no == "13337500" ~ cfs_source_elk_city,
      site_no == "13338500" ~ "observed",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-cfs_source_elk_city)
  
```

```{r prep-det-probs, include = FALSE}

# site detection efficiencies
comp_obs_study_df = comp_obs_df %>%
  filter(spawn_yr >= 2022)

# load configuration file
load("C:/Git/SnakeRiverFishStatus/data/configuration_files/site_config_LGR_20260116.rda") ; rm(crb_sites_sf, flowlines, sr_site_pops)

# sf clearwater parent-child table
sf_clwr_parent_child = tribble(
  ~parent, ~child,
  "SC1", "SC2",
  "SC2", "SC3",
  "SC3", "SC4",
  "SC4", "CRA"
)

# add nodes to parent-child
sf_clwr_pc_nodes = sf_clwr_parent_child %>%
  addParentChildNodes(.,  configuration = configuration)

# build node order
sf_node_order = buildNodeOrder(sf_clwr_pc_nodes)

# Function to estimate node efficiencies for a given species and year
estNodeEff_sy = function(df, spc, yr) {
  
  message("Estimating node efficiencies for ", spc, ", spawn year ", yr)
  
  estNodeEff(
    capHist_proc = df,
    node_order   = sf_node_order
  )
}

# estimate node efficiencies across species and spawn years
node_p_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ estNodeEff_sy(
      df  = .x,
      spc = .y$species,
      yr  = .y$spawn_yr
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r prep-cap-hists, include = FALSE}
#---------------------
# build capture histories

# function to convert compressed observations into capture histories, by species and year
buildCapHist_sy = function(df, spc, yr) {
  
  message("Creating capture histories for ", spc, ", spawn year ", yr)
  
  buildCapHist(
    filter_ch = df,
    parent_child = sf_clwr_parent_child,
    configuration = configuration,
    drop_nodes = T,
    keep_cols = c("tag_code")
  )
}

# create capture histories across species and spawn years
ch_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  filter(node %in% sf_node_order$node) %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ buildCapHist_sy(
      df  = .x,
      spc = .y$species,
      yr  = .y$spawn_yr
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# define the capture history columns
ch_cols = defineCapHistCols(
  parent_child  = sf_clwr_parent_child,
  configuration = configuration,
  use_rkm       = TRUE
)

```

This evaluation was conducted to quantify adult conversion rates since the installation of the SC3 and SC4 PIT-tag sites in 2021 and to establish a baseline for future monitoring efforts. These baseline estimates provide a framework for evaluating potential changes in passage success if actions are implemented to alleviate migration barriers within the study reach. The evaluation is ongoing and will continue to be refined as additional years of data become available and analyses evolve to address emerging questions.

## Study area

The study area encompasses the section of the South Fork Clearwater River near rkm 71 identified as a potential high-velocity migration barrier for steelhead (Figures \@ref(fig:study-map) and \@ref(fig:barrier-dv)). The evaluation relied on a series of instream PIT-tag detection sites (IPTDS) in the watershed to monitor movements of tagged steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon. Figure @ref(fig:study-map) and Table @ref(tab:sites-table) summarize the IPTDS locations used in this analysis, including their rkm measured upstream from the mouth of the South Fork Clearwater River.

# Evaluation

## Data

This evaluation used information from PIT-tagged adult steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon detected at IPTDS within the South Fork Clearwater River during upstream spawning migrations. The [DART](https://www.cbr.washington.edu/dart) database was queried using the `compressDART()` function in the R package `PITcleanr` to identify all returning adults detected at Lower Granite Dam (LGR) during spawn years 2022 - `r year(update_dttm)`. These detections were subsequently filtered to identify PIT-tagged adults later observed at any IPTDS within the South Fork Clearwater River (Table \@ref(tab:sites-table)). Adult detection efficiency at the LGR fish ladder is effectively 100%; therefore, PIT-tagged adults returning to the South Fork Clearwater River were assumed unlikely to be missed. To reduce the inclusion of post-spawn movements, kelts, shed tags, or other non-target detections, steelhead observations occurring after May 31 of the spawn year and sp/sum Chinook salmon observations occurring after September 15 were excluded from analyses. Additional biological information for adults trapped and PIT-tagged at LGR was obtained from the LGR trapping database. Additional datasets used in the evaluation, including stream discharge data, are described below. All data and code used in this evaluation are available on GitHub [here](https://github.com/NPTfisheries/SF_Clearwater_Passage).

## Conversion Rates

Annual conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 were first estimated for steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon (Table \@ref(tab:conv-rates)). The conversion rate represents the estimated proportion of PIT-tagged adults at SC3 that subsequently passed SC4. For example, during spawn year 2025, an estimated 334 steelhead passed SC3, of which 25 (7.5%) were estimated to subsequently pass SC4. Table \@ref(tab:conv-rates) summarizes the estimated number of PIT-tagged adults passing both SC3 and SC4, along with estimated conversion rates and associated standard errors. These estimates combine natural- and hatchery-origin adults from any release location.

```{r conv-rates, tab.cap = "Estimated tags passing SC3 and SC4, by species and spawn year, including estimated conversion rates."}
# calculate conversion rates with standard error
conversion_df = node_p_df %>%
  mutate(
    node = factor(node, levels = sf_node_order$node)
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  arrange(node, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    est_tags_prev = lag(est_tags_at_node),
    conv_rate = if_else(
      is.na(est_tags_prev) | est_tags_prev <= 0, 
      NA_real_,
      pmin(est_tags_at_node / est_tags_prev, 1)
    ),
    conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_prev),
    conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
    conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    node,
    est_tags_prev,
    obs_tags_at_node = tags_at_node,
    eff_est,
    eff_se,
    est_tags_at_node,
    conv_rate,
    conv_rate_se,
    conv_l95ci,
    conv_u95ci
  )

conv_tbl = conversion_df %>%
  filter(node == "SC4_D") %>%
  mutate(
    conv_rate = round(conv_rate * 100, 1),
    conv_rate_se = round(conv_rate_se * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(
    Species = species,
    `Spawn Year` = spawn_yr,
    `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_prev,
    `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_at_node,
    `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
    `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = "cccccc",
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

conv_tbl

```

Estimated conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 exceeded 80% for sp/sum Chinook salmon in all years evaluated. In contrast, estimated conversion rates for steelhead remained below 16% annually and averaged 13% across all years (Table \@ref(tab:conv-rates), Figure \@ref(fig:conv-rate-p)).

```{r conv-rate-p, fig.cap = "Estimated annual conversion rates (±95% confidence intervals) from SC3 to SC4 for PIT-tagged adult sp/sum Chinook salmon and steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River."}
# summary of conversion rates SC3 -> SC4
conversion_df %>%
  filter(node == "SC4_D") %>%
  transmute(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    conv_rate  = conv_rate * 100,
    conv_l95ci = conv_l95ci * 100,
    conv_u95ci = conv_u95ci * 100
  ) %>% 
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = spawn_yr,
      y = conv_rate,
      color = species,
      group = species
    )
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = seq(0, 100, 25),
    linewidth = 0.2,
    color = "grey85"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = conv_l95ci, ymax = conv_u95ci),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(conversion_df$spawn_yr))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x     = "Spawn Year",
    y     = "Conversion Rate",
    color = "Species",
    title = "Estimated Conversion from SC3 to SC4",
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "top",
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8))
  )

```

Interpretation of conversion rates may be influenced by biological and logistical factors. For example, most sp/sum Chinook salmon returning to the South Fork Clearwater River originate from natal tributaries located upstream of the high-velocity reach and are therefore generally expected to continue migrating through the reach to access spawning habitat. In contrast, many steelhead detected in the watershed originate from hatchery releases located downstream of the high-velocity reach. Differing release locations and origins (natural vs. hatchery) may create variation in adult migration behavior and route selection, potentially reducing apparent conversion rates for steelhead relative to Chinook salmon. Therefore, differences in origin and hatchery release location should be considered.

```{r prep-analysis-data}
# prep water level data from the sc4 probe
sc4_daily_depth = iptds_env_df %>%
  filter(reader.site.slug == "SC4",
         parameter.slug == "water_level") %>%
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value),
         date = date(read_at)) %>%
  group_by(reader.site.slug,
           parameter.slug,
           date) %>%
  summarise(mean = round(mean(value, na.rm = T), 2), .groups = "drop")

# query MRR sites
# mrr_df = queryMRRMeta()
# save(mrr_df, file = here("data/derived_data/mrr_metadata.rda"))
load(here("data/derived_data/mrr_metadata.rda"))

# compile observation, biological, environmental data, etc.
sf_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  select(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    tag_code,
    node,
    min_det
  ) %>%
  filter(node %in% sf_node_order$node) %>%
  # for instances where a tag has two compressed observations at a single node, keep first detection
  group_by(species, spawn_yr, tag_code, node) %>%
  slice_min(min_det, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # pivot wider to joining data
  group_by(species, spawn_yr, tag_code) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = node,
    values_from = c(min_det)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # join capture histories
  left_join(ch_df, by = c("species", "spawn_yr", "tag_code")) %>%
  # join some useful data from LGTrappingDB
  left_join(
    sf_clwr_lgr_df %>% select(-spawn_yr),
    by = c("species", "tag_code")
  ) %>%
  # join useful mark and release information from DART 
  left_join(dart_obs_df %>%
              select(tag_code,
                     mark_site,
                     rel_site,
                     mark_rear_type_name) %>%
              distinct(),
            by = "tag_code") %>%
  # join water level at SC4 using latest date that a fish was first observed at SC1, SC2, or SC3
  mutate(
    reach_arrival_date = as.Date(SC3)
  ) %>%
  left_join(sc4_daily_depth %>%
              select(date,
                     sc4_avg_daily_depth_m = mean),
            by = c("reach_arrival_date" = "date")) %>%
  # join daily average cfs from stites usgs gage 13338500
  left_join(sf_gage_pred_df %>%
              filter(site_no == 13338500) %>%
              select(date,
                     daily_cfs_stites = daily_mean_cfs),
            by = c("reach_arrival_date" = "date")) %>%
  # join daily average cfs from elk city usgs gage 13337500
  left_join(sf_gage_pred_df %>%
              filter(site_no == 13337500) %>%
              select(date,
                     daily_cfs_elk = daily_mean_cfs),
            by = c("reach_arrival_date" = "date")) %>%
  # did a fish pass SC3, SC4, and/or CRA?
  mutate(
    pass_sc3 = if_any(
      c(SC3, SC4_D, SC4_U, CRA_D, CRA_U),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    ),
    success = if_any(
      c(SC4_D, SC4_U, CRA_D, CRA_U),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  # some organizing
  select(species,
         spawn_yr,
         tag_code,
         cap_hist,
         pass_sc3,
         success,
         everything()) %>%
  left_join(mrr_df %>%
              select(siteCode,
                     type,
                     rkm),
            by = c("rel_site" = "siteCode")) %>%
  # fix some origins
  mutate(
    origin = case_when(
      str_detect(srr, "H$") ~ "H",
      str_detect(srr, "W$") ~ "W",
      mark_rear_type_name %in% c("H", "W", "U") ~ mark_rear_type_name,
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel_loc = case_when(
      # known upstream South Fork Clearwater groups
      str_detect(pbt_rel_group, regex("Newsome|RedR|CrookedR", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Upstream",
      # explicitly unknown / unassigned PBT groups
      pbt_rel_group %in% c("#N/A", "NG", "Unassigned-H", "Unassigned-W") ~ "Unknown",
      # other hatchery release groups
      str_detect(pbt_rel_group, "^\\d{4}") ~ "Downstream",
      # fallback to release site/type info if PBT group is not informative
      rel_site %in% c("REDP", "NEWSOC", "CROTRP") ~ "Upstream",
      type == "IntraDamReleaseSite"     ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ "Downstream"
    )
  ) %>%
  # filter out unknown origins and hatchery no-clip
  filter(
    origin != "U",
    !(origin == "H" & rel_loc == "Unknown")
  )

```

## Release Location

Because overall conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 may be influenced by juvenile release location relative to the high-velocity reach, conversion rates were evaluated separately for adults originating upstream and downstream juvenile release locations. Adults released upstream may be more likely to continue migrating through the reach to access natal or release-associated spawning areas, whereas adults released downstream may have less incentive to migrate upstream. For steelhead, most adults released upstream in this analysis originated from Newsome Creek juvenile releases. Table (\@ref(tab:rel-loc-tbl)) summarizes the inferred juvenile release location for all adults detected at IPTDS sites within the South Fork Clearwater River. Adults classified as having an unknown release location were typically fish newly PIT-tagged as adults at Bonneville or Lower Granite dams.

```{r rel-loc-tbl, message = F, tab.cap = "Summary of release location relative to the high-velocity reach for adult steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon observed at IPTDS sites in the South Fork Clearwater River, by year and rear type."}
# summarize tags by species, spawn_year, and release location
sf_df %>%
  count(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    origin,
    rel_loc,
    name = "n_tags"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = rel_loc,
    values_from = n_tags,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, spawn_yr, origin) %>%
  select(
    Species = species,
    `Spawn Year` = spawn_yr,
    `Rear Type` = origin,
    any_of(c("Upstream", "Downstream", "Unknown"))
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = "cccccc",
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

```

Because annual sample sizes of adult detections at SC4 were limited, data were aggregated across spawn years to estimate conversion rates by juvenile release location (Table \@ref(tab:rel-loc-conv); Figure \@ref(fig:rel-loc-p)). To date, a total of 1,242 adult steelhead originating from upstream releases have been detected at IPTDS within the South Fork Clearwater River, including 498 at SC3 and 54 at SC4. After accounting for IPTDS detection efficiency, the estimated conversion rate for upstream released steelhead was approximately 11%. This estimate was greater than conversion rates for downstream- and unknown-released steelhead, but remained substantially lower than estimated conversion rates for sp/sum Chinook salmon.

```{r rel-loc-conv, message = F, tab.cap = "Summary of conversion rates for adult sp/sum Chinook salmon and steelhead based on whether their juvenile release location was upstream or downstream of the barrier reach (or unknown)."}
# passage by release location
pass_by_rel_loc = sf_df %>%
  select(
    species,
    origin,
    spawn_yr,
    tag_code,
    pass_sc3,
    success,
    rel_loc
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    conversion_df %>%
      filter(node %in% c("SC3", "SC4_D")) %>%
      select(
        species,
        spawn_yr,
        node,
        eff_est,
        eff_se
      ) %>%
      pivot_wider(
        names_from = node,
        values_from = c(eff_est, eff_se)
      ),
    by = c("species", "spawn_yr")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sc3_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC3,
    sc4_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC4_D
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, rel_loc) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tags = n(),
    n_tags_sc3 = sum(pass_sc3, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tags_sc4 = sum(success, na.rm = TRUE),
    est_tags_sc3 = sum(if_else(pass_sc3, sc3_exp, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    est_tags_sc4 = sum(if_else(success, sc4_exp, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    conv_rate = if_else(
      est_tags_sc3 > 0,
      pmin(est_tags_sc4 / est_tags_sc3, 1),
      NA_real_
    ),
    conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_sc3),
    conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
    conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1)
  )

pass_by_rel_loc %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("conv"), ~ .x * 100),
    across(
      c(starts_with("conv"), starts_with("est")),
      ~ round(.x, 1)
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    Species = species,
    `Release Location` = rel_loc,
    `Obs Tags` = n_tags,
    `Obs Tags SC3` = n_tags_sc3,
    `Obs Tags SC4` = n_tags_sc4,
    `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_sc3,
    `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_sc4,
    `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
    `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = rep("c", ncol(.)),
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

```

## Elk City Discharge

Previous hydraulic modeling indicated that when discharge within the high-velocity reach exceeds approximately 1,000 cfs, at least one prominent hydraulic feature produces velocities exceeding the burst swimming capacity of a 90-cm steelhead [@Timm2018]. Earlier observations by NPT personnel further suggested that barrier conditions may begin to develop when discharge at the former Elk City gage exceeds approximately 600 cfs. Although streamflow is not directly monitored within the suspected barrier reach, previous work estimated that discharge in the reach is approximately two times greater than discharge measured at the Elk City gage [@Timm2018]. Under this assumption, a discharge of 1,000 cfs within the high-velocity reach would correspond to approximately 500 cfs at the Elk City gage. Therefore, conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 were estimated for periods when observed or estimated discharge at the Elk City gage was above or below 500 cfs (Table \@ref(tab:elk-cfs-conv-tbl); Figure \@ref(fig:elk-cfs-conv-p)). Because the exact discharge encountered by each adult steelhead while approaching the high-velocity reach is unknown, analyses used estimated discharge on the date each fish was first detected at SC3.

*NOTE: Because the Elk City gage is no longer operational, the relationship between discharge at the Elk City gage and the currently operational Stites gage was evaluated using overlapping historical daily mean discharge records (see Figure \@ref(fig:flow-corr)). Historical discharge data spanning from 2003, the first full year of the Elk City gage operation, through October 17, 2021, the final day of operation, were used to develop this relationship. The linear regression was then used to estimate daily mean discharge at the Elk City gage for recent years.*

Estimated conversion rates above and below 500 cfs at the Elk City gage (approximately equivalent to 1,000 cfs within the reach) were not substantially different (Table \@ref(tab:elk-cfs-conv-tbl); Figure \@ref(fig:elk-cfs-conv-p)).

```{r elk-cfs-conv-tbl, tab.cap = "Summary of estimated SC3-to-SC4 conversion rates, by species and release location, based on estimated discharge at the former Elk City gage on the date fish arrived at SC3."}
# flow to evaluate
cfs = 500

# passage by estimated Elk City cfs
pass_by_cfs = sf_df %>%
  filter(pass_sc3 == TRUE) %>%
  select(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    tag_code,
    origin,
    pass_sc3,
    success,
    rel_loc,
    daily_cfs_elk
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cfs_elk_bin = case_when(
      is.na(daily_cfs_elk) ~ NA_character_,
      daily_cfs_elk >= cfs ~ paste0(">= ", cfs, " cfs"),
      daily_cfs_elk <  cfs ~ paste0("< " , cfs, " cfs")
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    conversion_df %>%
      filter(node %in% c("SC3", "SC4_D")) %>%
      select(
        species,
        spawn_yr,
        node,
        eff_est,
        eff_se
      ) %>%
      pivot_wider(
        names_from = node,
        values_from = c(eff_est, eff_se)
      ),
    by = c("species", "spawn_yr")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sc3_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC3,
    sc4_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC4_D
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, rel_loc, cfs_elk_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tags = n(),
    n_tags_sc3 = sum(pass_sc3, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tags_sc4 = sum(success, na.rm = TRUE),
    est_tags_sc3 = sum(if_else(pass_sc3, sc3_exp, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    est_tags_sc4 = sum(if_else(success, sc4_exp, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    conv_rate = if_else(
      est_tags_sc3 > 0,
      pmin(est_tags_sc4 / est_tags_sc3, 1),
      NA_real_
    ),
    conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_sc3),
    conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
    conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1)
  )

pass_by_cfs %>%
  filter(!is.na(cfs_elk_bin)) %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("conv"), ~ .x * 100),
    across(starts_with("est"),  ~ round(.x, 0)),
    across(starts_with("conv"), ~ round(.x, 1))
  ) %>%
  arrange(species, rel_loc, desc(cfs_elk_bin)) %>%
  select(
    Species = species,
    `Release Location` = rel_loc,
    `Est Discharge at SC3 Arrival` = cfs_elk_bin,
    #`Obs Tags` = n_tags,
    #`Obs Tags SC3` = n_tags_sc3,
    #`Obs Tags SC4` = n_tags_sc4,
    `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_sc3,
    `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_sc4,
    `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
    `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = rep("c", ncol(.)),
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

```

```{r elk-cfs-conv-p, fig.cap = "Estimated conversion rates (±95% confidence intervals) from SC3 to SC4 for PIT-tagged adult steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River, by release location and estimated discharge at the Elk City gage on the date fish arrived at SC3."}

<!--
# Logistic Regression

Finally, we evaluated the probability of an adult being detected at SC4 (given it arrived at SC3) depending on species, release location, and predicted flow (cfs) at the previous Elk City gage at the time of last detection. To do so, we fit a logistic regression model using species, release location, and estimated flow as covariates and probability of arriving at SC4 as the response variable. A fish that successfully arrived at SC4 was a "success" = 1 whereas a fish only seen at SC3 was "success" = 0. Three nested logistic regression models were fit and compared using likelihood ratio tests: (1) a full model including species, release location, and stream flow; (2) a reduced model with species and release location; and (3) a baseline model with species only. Figure \@ref(fig:lm-p) shows that the best-fitting model included only species as a covariate, with Chinook exhibiting a predicted probability of 0.81 and steelhead 0.12 for successfully passing upstream.
-->

```{r lm, results = "hide", eval = F}
library(purrr)
library(broom)
library(AICcmodavg)

# prep data
lm_df = sf_df %>%
  select(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    pass_sc3,
    success,
    rel_loc,
    SC3,
    last_det_dwn,
    daily_cfs_stites,
    lgr_fl_mm
  ) %>%
  filter(
    species == "Steelhead",
    pass_sc3 == TRUE,
    !is.na(SC3),
    rel_loc != "Downstream"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    SC3          = as.Date(SC3),
    success      = as.integer(success),
    rel_loc      = factor(rel_loc),
    arrival_day  = yday(SC3)
  ) %>%
  filter(month(SC3) %in% 1:6) %>%
  drop_na(
    success,
    arrival_day,
    daily_cfs_stites
    # lgr_fl_mm
  )

# scaling values
arrival_mean = mean(lm_df$arrival_day)
arrival_sd   = sd(lm_df$arrival_day)

flow_mean = mean(lm_df$daily_cfs_stites)
flow_sd   = sd(lm_df$daily_cfs_stites)

length_mean = mean(lm_df$lgr_fl_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
length_sd   = sd(lm_df$lgr_fl_mm, na.rm = TRUE)

# standardize covariates
lm_df = lm_df %>%
  mutate(
    arrival_std = (arrival_day - arrival_mean) / arrival_sd,
    flow_std    = (daily_cfs_stites - flow_mean) / flow_sd,
    length_std  = (lgr_fl_mm - length_mean) / length_sd
  )


# candidate covariates
covariates = c(
  "arrival_std",
  "flow_std"
  # "length_std"
)

pred_sets = unlist(
  map(
    0:length(covariates),
    \(k) combn(covariates, k, simplify = FALSE)
  ),
  recursive = FALSE
)

formulas = map(
  pred_sets,
  \(x) reformulate(
    termlabels = x,
    response = "success"
  )
)

# fit models
mod_list = map(
  formulas,
  \(f) glm(
    formula = f,
    data    = lm_df,
    family  = binomial(link = "logit")
  )
)

names(mod_list) = map_chr(
  formulas,
  \(x) {
    terms = attr(stats::terms(x), "term.labels")
    
    if (length(terms) == 0) {
      "null"
    } else {
      paste(terms, collapse = " + ")
    }
  }
)

# model selection
mod_sel_df = tibble(
  model = names(mod_list),
  k     = map_int(mod_list, \(x) length(coef(x))),
  AICc  = map_dbl(mod_list, AICc)
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_AICc = AICc - min(AICc),
    weight = exp(-0.5 * delta_AICc) /
      sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_AICc))
  ) %>%
  arrange(AICc)

mod_sel_df

best_mod_name = mod_sel_df$model[1]
lm_mod_best = mod_list[[best_mod_name]]
summary(lm_mod_best)

# coefficient table
lm_mod_coef = tidy(
  lm_mod_best,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  exponentiate = TRUE
)

lm_mod_coef

# arrival-date prediction plot; flow held at mean, i.e., flow_std = 0
pred_arrival_df = tibble(
  arrival_day = seq(
    min(lm_df$arrival_day),
    max(lm_df$arrival_day),
    by = 1
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    arrival_std = (arrival_day - arrival_mean) / arrival_sd,
    flow_std = 0,
    length_std = 0,
    arrival_date = as.Date("2000-01-01") + arrival_day - 1
  )

pred = predict(
  lm_mod_best,
  newdata = pred_arrival_df,
  type = "link",
  se.fit = TRUE
)

pred_arrival_df = pred_arrival_df %>%
  mutate(
    fit = plogis(pred$fit),
    lwr = plogis(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    upr = plogis(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  )

arrival_p = pred_arrival_df %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = arrival_date,
      y = fit
    )
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
    alpha = 0.18,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_labels = "%b %d",
    date_breaks = "2 weeks"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Arrival date at SC3",
    y = "Predicted probability of passing SC4",
    title = "Predicted steelhead passage probability by arrival timing"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

arrival_p

# flow prediction plot; arrival held at mean, i.e., arrival_std = 0
pred_flow_df = tibble(
  daily_cfs_stites = seq(
    min(lm_df$daily_cfs_stites),
    max(lm_df$daily_cfs_stites),
    length.out = 100
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    flow_std = (daily_cfs_stites - flow_mean) / flow_sd,
    arrival_std = 0,
    length_std = 0
  )

pred = predict(
  lm_mod_best,
  newdata = pred_flow_df,
  type = "link",
  se.fit = TRUE
)

pred_flow_df = pred_flow_df %>%
  mutate(
    fit = plogis(pred$fit),
    lwr = plogis(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    upr = plogis(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  )

flow_p = pred_flow_df %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = daily_cfs_stites,
      y = fit
    )
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
    alpha = 0.18,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Daily mean discharge at Stites (cfs)",
    y = "Predicted probability of passing SC4",
    title = "Predicted steelhead passage probability by discharge"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

flow_p

# observed relationship between arrival timing and flow
arrival_flow_p = lm_df %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = arrival_day,
      y = daily_cfs_stites
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 244, by = 30),
    labels = \(x) format(as.Date("2000-01-01") + x - 1, "%b %d")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Arrival date at SC3",
    y = "Daily mean discharge at Stites (cfs)",
    title = "Relationship between steelhead arrival timing and discharge"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

arrival_flow_p

cor(
  lm_df$arrival_day,
  lm_df$daily_cfs_stites,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

```

# Discussion

Previous studies have indicated that a partial velocity barrier to adult steelhead passage may occur near rkm 71, at least at higher flows [@Timm2018], and that the majority of steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River likely spawn below there [@Cleary2019]. Based on PIT-tagged adult returns in recent years, it is difficult to discern whether the high-velocity reach hinders or prevents upstream passage for adult steelhead; however, conversion rates for steelhead are remarkably lower than those for sp/sum Chinook salmon. Conversion rates for adult steelhead from SC3 to SC4 is below 16% in all years, including for individuals from juvenile releases from Newsome Creek.

The number of PIT-tagged juvenile steelhead within Newsome Creek releases was increased starting in spring 2022 (Table \@ref(tab:juv-releases)); 1-ocean adults from spring 2022 releases began returning to the South Fork Clearwater River in spring 2024 and we did observe a 3-fold increase in adults returning from those releases as expected. The first two-ocean adults returned in the spring 2025. Continued returns from planned future releases will increase our sample sizes and observations and improve our ability to evaluate conversion rates in future years. Regardless, we have established monitoring for if and when restoration actions take place to address potential passage issues due to high stream velocities.

Our evaluation used season-long estimates of detection efficiencies to expand observed tags into estimates of tags passing each IPTDS, which in turn was used to estimate conversion rates. We recognize that detection efficiencies of IPTDS can be influenced by factors including river depth or dishcarge; however, we used season-wide estimates largely due to lower sample sizes at more extreme flows. We will explore stratifying estimates of detection efficiency for future years if increased PIT-tag returns allows.

node_p_df %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("eff")), ~ round(. * 100, 1)) %>%
  filter(!node %in% c("SC4_U", "CRA_D", "CRA_U")) %>%
  arrange(species, node, spawn_yr) %>%
  select(Species = species,
         `Spawn Year` = spawn_yr,
         Site = node,
         `Obs Tags` = tags_at_node,
         `Obs Tags Above` = tags_above_node,
         `Resighted Tags` = tags_resighted,
         `Detection Prob (%)` = eff_est,
         `Detection SE` = eff_se) %>%
  kable(booktabs = T,
        align = "cccccccc",
        label = NA) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = F,
                position = "center",
